rules.title: Prohibited efficacy and safety language
rules.description: Promotional material must not state or imply that an Acme product cures the condition it treats, that a result is guaranteed, or that the product is completely safe or free of risk.

params.suggested_fix: Describe the observed effect using the labelled endpoint and timepoint instead.

examples.text: Zelvoran can cure plaque psoriasis in most adults.
Zelvoran is completely safe for long-term use.
In a 16-week randomised trial, 68.4% of adults treated with Zelvoran achieved PASI-75 compared with 9.2% receiving placebo.
examples.note: Labelled result with comparator and timepoint.

examples.text: Reviewers discussed the paper "Toward a cure for plaque psoriasis" at the congress.
examples.note: Banned term inside a quoted title is a citation, not a claim.

examples.text: Patients should book a manicure before starting treatment.
examples.note: Word-boundary check - "manicure" must not trip the "cure" term.

rules.source_ref: Acme Brand and Promotional Code, clause 9

rules.title: Typical results in patient-directed material
rules.description: Patient-directed material must not imply that the results described are typical of all patients unless the approved label supports that characterisation, and must direct the reader to a healthcare professional.

params.guidance: Look for language suggesting a reader should expect the described outcome themselves, such as "you will", "most people see", "typical results", or a testimonial presented without qualification. A response rate stated with its population, comparator and timepoint is not a violation. Absence of a direction to speak to a healthcare professional is a violation only when the piece also implies a personal expectation of benefit.

examples.text: Most people see clear skin within weeks. You can expect the same.
examples.note: Asserts a personal expectation of benefit with no qualification.

examples.text: Zelvoran works for everyone with plaque psoriasis.
examples.note: Universal claim unsupported by any response rate.

examples.text: In a 16-week study, 68.4% of adults treated with Zelvoran achieved at least a 75% improvement in their psoriasis score, compared with 9.2% who received placebo. Individual results vary. Talk to your doctor about whether Zelvoran is right for you.
examples.note: Labelled result with comparator and timepoint, qualified, and directs to a clinician.

rules.source_ref: Acme Brand and Promotional Code, clause 10

rules.title: Compliance with the Acme Brand and Promotional Code
rules.description: Promotional material must comply with the Acme Brand and Promotional Code. A finding under this rule must quote the exact clause of the Code that the material breaches.

clauses: A result observed in a subgroup must be described as a subgroup result, naming the subgroup. A subgroup figure must never be presented as the result in the overall population.
A claim that an Acme product is better than, more effective than, or preferable to another therapy requires a head-to-head clinical trial against that named therapy.
Claims about how long an effect lasts must not extend beyond the longest timepoint for which data exist.
Every claim of efficacy or safety must carry a reference to the specific study supporting it. The cited study must report the endpoint, population and timepoint stated in the claim.

examples.text: Nearly 6 in 10 adults achieved PASI-90 with Zelvoran at Week 16. Please see full Prescribing Information.
examples.note: 58.1% is the prior-biologic subgroup result; the overall population was 44.2%. Breaches the subgroup clause.

examples.text: Two years of sustained clear skin with Zelvoran. Please see full Prescribing Information.
examples.note: No data beyond Week 52 exist. Breaches the durability clause.

examples.text: In ZEL-302, 44.2% of adults treated with Zelvoran achieved PASI-90 at Week 16, compared with 4.8% receiving placebo (Reference 2). Please see full Prescribing Information.
examples.note: Overall-population result, correctly attributed and referenced.
